title: Reveal and fold become one toggle; Copy link removed

history.detail:
PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, Sprint 56. Commit 4f979c6 on devteam2/sprint-56, worktree clean. Verdict: PASS.

Sprint file: re-read fresh. Its only difference from main's copy is the lifecycle-owned status: line, so there is no amendment. No criterion claims something arrives between two versions.

Handoff: read via git show 4f979c6:docs/handoffs/sprint-56.md. Round 1 quotes "VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0".
My own re-run in the worktree: npm run verify ended with exit=0. Test Files 56 passed, Tests 640 passed, lint 0 errors and 3 warnings.

R1, met. SavedHoroscope's details now holds only its summary, and it is the first child of .readingFooter. The summary wraps one .castButton span, which has two label spans. CSS hides one by the details' own [open] state, with display: none, so only the current label is in the accessible name. .revealFold and .revealFolded are gone from both the TSX and the CSS.

R2, met. It keeps native details/summary: no JS, no request, no URL change. The summary exposes expanded or collapsed natively, plus aria-controls naming the text. The text stays in the server HTML in both states.
The folded hiding rule is keyed on :not([open]) inside :has(), so a browser without :has() fails open (shows the text), not closed.
The handoff's probe shows open and fold working with script execution disabled. The no-JS screenshot (date-390-open-no-js.png) confirms it.

R3, met. Confirmed from the markup and CSS. The DOM order is: text block, then .readingFooter, which holds details/summary, then .revealControls (display: contents, holding the date link or Try again), then the note.
grep for order:, row-reverse, column-reverse and tabindex in reading.module.css and the TSX finds no reordering. So DOM order equals visual order equals focus order. toggle-pages.test.ts asserts the focus order on both routes.

R4, met. The note is in both states. The date link is on /reading/[id] at both widths, now one link with no desktop/mobile duplicate. Try again goes into controls after a failed generation. The header status and IdleBlock :has() rules were updated from the direct-child form to the descendant form, which is correct since the details is no longer a direct child.
The reveal-landing and rise tests pass. paragraphRise is unchanged and is still applied to the paragraphs.

R5, met. Sprint 38's details-sticky workaround is removed. With .revealPanel display: contents, the .readingFooter row is a direct flex item of the section or form in both states, so the existing phone rule (position: sticky; bottom: 0) applies.
The screenshot reading-390-open-mid-text-sticky.png shows the toggle stuck at the bottom mid-text. The .castButton phone rule (min-height 44px, border-box) applies, and .reveal is flex: 1.
The handoff explains the date page at 390, folded at load (13px below the fold), as Sprint 38's existing containing-block behaviour. It measures the same in the unsaved state, so I accept it as not a regression.

R6, met. grep -rniE "copy link|clipboard" app lib gives exit=1. CopyLinkButton, DateLinks and the .mobileWrittenFooter CSS are gone, and the only matches for those names are the new tests asserting their absence. useState is still imported, and it's still used by prevPending and justWrote. The date page's open footer holds only the toggle and the note.

R7, met. The unsaved button path and DisabledReadingSection without a horoscope are unchanged. DisabledReadingSection's saved path now passes note.
This is the 5-line edit in ReadingView.tsx, Sprint 55's file. The sprint file required flagging it to Master Controller first. The handoff says the user approved it ("Proceed, edit ReadingView", 26 Nov 2026), and the edit is in a different function from Sprint 55's. Sprint 55's code is already on this branch's base, bd51b50, so this branch does not conflict with it.

R8, met. The new toggle-pages.test.ts runs through the real page components on both routes. It covers:
- folded and open labels, with exactly one summary;
- the fold label appearing once in the HTML;
- the summary placed after the last paragraph;
- focus order;
- the note in both states;
- the date link;
- no copy link;
- CSS guards.
The visibleWhen helper models the hiding rules by balanced-tag removal, which is reasonable. The updated Sprint 33 tests are listed in the handoff. Sprint 38 had no sticky test to update, so the CSS guard covers R5.

R9, met. I opened reading-1280-open, date-1280-folded, reading-390-open-mid-text-sticky and date-390-open-no-js, and all four match the handoff.

Dev Team's questions:
1. 182 vs 184px at 1280. Acceptable. Every computed style matches. The 2px is a flex-shrink result, not styling, and R1 asks for the same styling, not the same pixel width.
2. The screen reader reaches the text before the toggle. Acceptable. R1 and R3 together require the toggle below the text, and aria-controls is present.

For Master Controller (not blocking, not routed as a prerequisite):
- Find-in-page no longer reaches folded text, because it is display: none outside the details. Sprint 33 never required it.
- Open, the text now sits at the section's normal 20px gap below "The reading" heading. The old fold control used to sit between them.
- The 3 lint warnings in the sprint-45 and sprint-46 evidence scripts are STILL unowned. No recorded decision accepts them.

Human prerequisites: none.
commit=2398f13 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 2398f13a8c7e79bf44b98674e2d8ed3659a88004 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

FAIL: LiveQA live test, Sprint 56, round 1. Verdict: FAIL, on step 7 (R10). Steps 1 to 6 pass.
Environment: production https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-11-26 ~16:35-17:00Z. Headless Chromium (Playwright 1.59.1 with the cached chromium_headless_shell-1248), with JavaScript both on and off. Read-only: no horoscope generated, no form submitted.

DEPLOYED BUILD: /api/health/db reports 4c1cb63 (isLocal false). The shipped commit is 2398f13. git diff --stat 2398f13 4c1cb63 touches only docs/sprints (the Sprint 55 done file, registry.json, and the sprint-55 and sprint-56 state files), so the live app code is exactly 2398f13.
SPRINT FILE: R10 and LiveQA step 7 were amended in after the ship (f567e08). The shipped code predates them. The user asked, in this session, that this verdict include step 7, and it does. Saved reading used: /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d (20 July 1969).

STEP 1, /date/1969-07-20 at 1280: PASS.
- Folded: one summary, label "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE", 0 paragraphs visible, toggle at the bottom of the reading. Its castButton has border 1px solid, padding 11px 18px, 10.5px IBM Plex Mono, uppercase, letter-spacing 1.89px, 182x52.
- After a click: open, label "FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY", 3 paragraphs visible. The toggle top (doc 1101.7) is below the last paragraph bottom (doc 1078.7). The computed style is identical except the width (195x52).
- The only visible fold control is that summary, so the old small one is gone.
- A second click: folded, "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE", 0 paragraphs.
- The URL is unchanged, with 0 document or fetch requests across both toggles. No console errors.

STEP 2, keyboard: PASS.
- On /date/1969-07-20 it took 7 Tabs to reach the SUMMARY. Enter opens it ("FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY", 3 paragraphs). The next Tab goes to the date-picker INPUT, since the date page has no footer link by design (R6). Shift+Tab returns to the SUMMARY, and Space folds it ("REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE", 0 paragraphs).
- On /reading/0b01c79f it took 5 Tabs. Enter opens it, and the next Tab goes to A href=/date/1969-07-20 "GO TO THIS DATE". Space folds it.
- Expanded state, from the Chromium accessibility tree (CDP): role DisclosureTriangle, name "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE", expanded false; then name "FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY", expanded true.

STEP 3, 390: PASS.
- "copy link" does not appear in the body text on any page tested, at either width, with or without JS.
- Folded, with "The reading" heading 120px above the fold: the footer is position sticky, and the toggle sits at top 788, bottom 832 with vh 844. It's hit-testable, with a 44px touch target. This holds on both routes, with and without JS.
- Open, scrolled so the text runs below the screen (last paragraph bottom at 1024, vh 844): the toggle "FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY" stays at bottom 832 and is hit-testable. Clicking it from mid-text folds it.
- scrollWidth is 390.

STEP 4, /reading/0b01c79f at 1280 and 390: PASS. Toggle behaviour matches step 1, and the open footer holds toggle, "GO TO THIS DATE" (/date/1969-07-20), and the note, at both widths.

STEP 5, JavaScript disabled: PASS. Steps 1 and 3 repeated with javaScriptEnabled false gave the same labels, paragraph counts, sticky positions and hit tests as with JS.

STEP 6, no saved horoscope, markup only: PASS.
- /date/1983-11-26 and /date/1979-11-26: 0 summary elements. "The reading" holds a POST form with button type=submit "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE", class castButton, badge "NOT REVEALED YET", and the IdleBlock text. Not clicked.
- (/date/2008-11-26 already has a saved horoscope, with 1 summary, so it doesn't apply.)

STEP 7 / R10, gap from header row to first text: FAIL.
I measured from the header row's bottom (sectionHeader / readingHeader) to the top of the first text line box (Range rect), plus the element box gap in brackets.
- "What happened" to its first eventText: 21px [19] at 1280, 18px [17] at 390, on both routes.
- "The reading" OPEN, to the first paragraph: 3px [0] at 1280, 3px [0] at 390, on both routes. That is 18 and 15px short, against a 2px tolerance. The screenshot shows the first line sitting directly under the heading line.
- "The reading" FOLDED, to IdleBlock idleText: 13px [10] at 1280 and 390, on both routes. That is 8 and 5px short of What happened, so R10's second bullet also applies to the folded IdleBlock.
- Not measured: the Sprint 39 accuracy note, since no unmatched date has a saved horoscope to open.

SECOND ISSUE, for Dev Team or Master Controller to judge against R1's "styled exactly like" and step 1's "in the same style": the open label wraps where the folded one never does.
- /date/1969-07-20 at 1280: "FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY" sits on 2 lines (195px wide); "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE" is 1 line.
- /reading/0b01c79f at 1280: 3 lines ("FOLD THE / HOROSCOPE / AWAY"), button 141x66, beside "GO TO THIS DATE" and the note, while the folded toggle is 182x52.
- /reading/0b01c79f at 390: 3 lines, 140x72, while the folded toggle is 326x44 and "GO TO THIS DATE" takes the wider share of the row.
The computed styles match, so this is width or flex sizing, not styling. It still looks like a different, cramped button in hand. Screenshots: rd-1280-open.png, rd-390-open.png, date-1280-js-open.png.

OBSERVATION, not a defect: opening the toggle on /reading/ fired 2 GET fetches, /date/1969-07-20?_rsc=..., when the newly visible "GO TO THIS DATE" link appeared. That's Next.js link prefetch, not the toggle. The date page fired 0 requests, folding fired 0, and toggling works with JS off, so R2's guarantee holds.

Screenshots (session scratchpad, s56/): date-1280-js-folded/open, date-1280-nojs-folded/open, date-390-*-folded-sticky, sticky-folded-*, open-midtext-*, rd-1280-folded/open, rd-390-folded/open, step6-2008-11-26.png.

Provenance: this is a deployed web app, so verify-release-content.sh does not apply. The deploy was verified through the health endpoint's commit and the bookkeeping-only diff.

To fix: R10 spacing, open and folded, on both routes and at both widths. Then decide on the wrapping open label.

NOTE: sprint 56's file has changed since QA1's PASS (audited hash d5f5edd91548..., current f512b9ba9843...). Recorded, not refused — see this function's own comment for why. PASS: QA1 live-loop audit, Sprint 56 round 2. Commit 06f093f680102972eb371651e3c9c962478cae30 on devteam2/sprint-56, worktree clean. Verdict: PASS.

SPRINT FILE: re-read fresh, including the R10 amendment (f567e08, added after the ship from the user's own review), its acceptance line, and LiveQA step 7.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN ROUND-1 RECORD: my gate-1 notes recorded the open text sitting at "the section's normal 20px gap below The reading heading" as not a defect. That was wrong. I did not notice that with generation on, the panel is inside a block-level form, so the section's flex gap never applied there. The real box gap was 0, as LiveQA measured. This audit replaces that reading.

WHAT CHANGED vs the shipped 2398f13: git diff --stat 2398f13 06f093f -- app lib shows only reading.module.css (+20/-4) and toggle-pages.test.ts (+13). The rest is docs/handoffs. No TSX changed.

R10, met. The change is spacing only:
- .readingSection's gap is now a variable, at the same values (20px, and 14px on phones).
- A new rule gives the first block after the header inside the form a top margin equal to that gap: .readingSection form .idleBlock and .readingSection form .revealText.
- .idleBlock and .accuracyNote drop their 10px top padding. Outside a form, that padding used to stack on the section gap, giving 33px.
No toggle, text, header, font, colour or width rule changed.
Handoff distances (raw JSON in docs/handoffs/sprint-56/round-2/, which I spot-checked against the table):
- open and folded, both routes: 23 against 21 at 1280, and 17 against 18 at 390;
- unsaved idle and generation-disabled states: the same;
- accuracy note: 23 at 1280, and 16 against 18 at 390, exactly at the 2px tolerance.
Before: 3 open and 13 folded, which matches LiveQA's production numbers.
The selectors are scoped tightly enough. The DatePicker's form has no idleBlock or revealText, and the no-form path gets no double spacing. I opened round-2/date-1280-open.png, and the space under the header is restored.

VERIFY: handoff round 2 quotes "VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0". My own re-run in the worktree also exited 0: 56 files and 642 tests, 0 lint errors, 3 warnings. The 2 new CSS guards are string-level checks on the rules, which is adequate for a CSS-only change. The round-1 behavioural tests pass unchanged.

LiveQA's second issue (the wrapping open label): Dev Team decided not to change it, with measurements. I agree it's outside this round. R10 says "Nothing else about the toggle ... changes", and the folded label also wraps at 1280 (182x52, 2 lines), so R1's "styled exactly like" still holds. Whether to stack the open footer on phones is Master Controller's call, as a follow-up.

FINDING FOR MASTER CONTROLLER (not R10 as written; route it before LiveQA round 2):
This fix widens the busy-state jump. Inside the form, the unsaved IdleBlock now starts 20px below the header row (14 on phones): the new margin-top, plus padding 0. The BusyBlock that replaces it on click ("Revealing…") is not in the new selector and keeps padding 6px 0 2px, so it starts 6px below.
- Before this fix: idle 10 against busy 6, a 4px shift.
- Now: a 14px shift at 1280, and 8px on phones. The content moves up when generation starts.
- The busy text also sits 6px under the header, the same kind of flush spacing the user objected to for the open text.
Derived from the CSS: .idleBlock padding-top 0 plus margin-top var(--reading-gap), against .busyBlock padding 6px 0 2px, with the form a plain block.
The handoff says plainly that it did not check busy, and R10 doesn't name it, so this is not a FAIL of R10. Master Controller should decide whether R10 covers the busy block. It's a one-selector change (add .readingSection form .busyBlock and drop its top padding) if so.
Also unchecked, per the handoff: date.module.css .unavailableText (the outage notice) still has padding 10px 0 4px outside a form.

STILL UNOWNED: the 3 lint warnings in the sprint-45 and sprint-46 evidence scripts. No recorded decision accepts them.

Human prerequisites: none.
This live-loop PASS does not replace LiveQA's round-2 retest, which must re-run step 7. | commit=06f093f680102972eb371651e3c9c962478cae30

target_index=1 | target_event=audit | target_ts=2026-11-26T16:22:29+00:00 | QA1 correction to event [1] (my gate-1 audit of 4f979c6). Under "For Master Controller", I wrote that the open text "now sits at the section's normal 20px gap below The reading heading". That is factually wrong.

With generation enabled, the panel renders inside a form, which is a plain block. The section's flex gap therefore never applied there. The real box gap was 0px, about 3px to the text, as LiveQA measured in event [4].

The PASS verdict on R1 to R9 is unaffected. The spacing became R10, and it was fixed in 06f093f. My live-loop audit of that commit is in event [6].
commit=06f093f | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 06f093f680102972eb371651e3c9c962478cae30 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: LiveQA live test, Sprint 56, round 2. Verdict: PASS. All 7 LiveQA steps pass, including step 7 / R10, which failed in round 1.
Environment: production https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-11-26 ~17:10-17:25Z. Headless Chromium (Playwright 1.59.1 with the cached chromium_headless_shell-1248), JS on and off. Read-only: nothing generated or submitted.

DEPLOYED BUILD: /api/health/db reports b0f8de7 (isLocal false). The reshipped commit is 06f093f. git diff --stat 06f093f b0f8de7 touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-56.json, so the live app code is exactly 06f093f. The app-code change since round 1 (ef38b50..06f093f) is app/reading/[id]/reading.module.css and a test file only.
Method: I re-ran round 1's exact scripts unchanged, plus one added gap probe. Saved reading: /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d.

STEP 7 / R10: PASS. Measured from the header row bottom to the first text line box top (Range rect). The target is the "What happened" / events heading row to its first eventText.
- OPEN, first paragraph, /date/1969-07-20 and /reading/0b01c79f: 23 at 1280 (target 21, +2); 17 at 390 (target 18, -1). Round 1 was 3 and 3.
- FOLDED, IdleBlock idleText, both routes: 23 at 1280 (+2); 17 at 390 (-1). Round 1 was 13 and 13.
- UNSAVED IdleBlock, /date/1983-11-26 (inside the form): 23 at 1280 (target 21, +2); 17 at 390 (target 18, -1).
- Sprint 39 accuracy note (no form): /date/1950-03-15 and /date/2026-11-26 give 23 at 1280 (target 21 under "Other years with events on ...", +2) and 16 at 390 (target 18, -2).
Every state is within 2px. Two cases sit exactly at the tolerance: +2 at 1280, and -2 for the accuracy note at 390. These match the handoff's own round 2 table exactly.
Screenshot rd-1280-open.png shows clear space between "The reading" and the first paragraph.

STEPS 1-6: PASS, re-verified with identical results to round 1.
- Step 1, /date/1969-07-20 at 1280: folded "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE", 182x52, 0 paragraphs. Click: "FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY", 195x52, 3 paragraphs, toggle below the text. Click again folds it. URL unchanged, 0 requests, no console errors.
- Step 2: the date page takes 7 Tabs to the SUMMARY; Enter opens it; Tab goes to the picker INPUT (no footer link there by design); Space folds it. /reading takes 5 Tabs; Enter opens it; Tab goes to A /date/1969-07-20 "GO TO THIS DATE"; Space folds it. The AX tree shows DisclosureTriangle, expanded false, then true.
- Step 3, 390: no "copy link" text anywhere. Folded with the heading 120px above the fold: footer position sticky, toggle bottom 832 of vh 844, hit-testable, 44px tall. Open with text running below the screen (last paragraph bottom 1024): toggle bottom 832, hit-testable. Clicking it mid-text folds it. scrollWidth is 390.
- Step 4, /reading at 1280 and 390: same toggle behaviour; the open footer holds the toggle, "GO TO THIS DATE" and the note.
- Step 5, JS off: steps 1 and 3 give identical results.
- Step 6: /date/1983-11-26 and /date/1979-11-26 show 0 summary elements and a POST form with submit "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE" (castButton), badge "NOT REVEALED YET". Not clicked.

CARRIED OVER FROM ROUND 1, NOW DECIDED: the open label still wraps. It's 2 lines on the date page at 1280 (195x52), and 3 lines on /reading at 1280 (141x66) and 390 (140x72). The round 2 handoff records Dev Team's measured decision to keep it as is: giving the toggle its natural width pushes "Go to this date" to 3 lines instead. QA1's live-loop audit passed that. I recorded it as a judgement call in round 1, not a criterion failure, so it does not block this verdict.
OBSERVATION, unchanged: opening on /reading triggers 2 Next.js prefetches of /date/1969-07-20?_rsc=... for the newly visible link. The toggle makes no requests of its own and works with JS off.
